optionReasons.saa-ini-266:option:0: st1 is HDD of THROUGHPUT sequential — latency and IOPS worse than SSD; the statement reverses the reality.
optionReasons.saa-ini-266:option:2: sc1 is the HDD colder LENTO — bad for production bank I/O.
optionReasons.saa-ini-266:option:3: Magnetic 'standard' is old generation — SSDs surpass it just in Random I/O.

finalJustifications: Because gp3 (until 16.000 IOPS, cost-benefit) covers most banks, and i2 Block Express (up to 256.000 IOPS, 99,999% sustainability) responds to critical mission.
Because gp3 and i2 are the only volumes EBS which accept cryptography at rest, the production database requirement.
Because the Io2 Block Express rotates inside the memory RAM of the physical host, the origin of 256.000 IOPS Critical mission announcements.
Because the gp3 folds the IOPS automatically when the database grows, following the demand without reproducing the volume.

optionReasons.saa-ini-275:option:0: RRS is class LEGADA discontinued — and reducing redundancy of active logs is not the objective.
optionReasons.saa-ini-275:option:1: Expiration is just the PONTA final — does not alone make intermediate transitions to cheaper classes.
optionReasons.saa-ini-275:option:2: Intelligent-Tiering optimizes unpredictable access — here the pattern is CONHECIDO (30/90/180 days): lifecycle with transitions and expiration is more direct and cheap (no monitoring fee).

finalJustifications: Because the Lifecycle Policy program completes the way: Standard-IA to 30 days, Glacier to the 90 and automatic exclusion to 180 — Total optimization without intervention.
Because Lifecycle Policy compacts the old logs before moving them, reducing the volume charged in each class transition.
Because Lifecycle Policy replicates the logs to another region before deleting, preserving the required copy of the compliance.
Because Lifecycle Policy informs the team to approve each transition, maintaining human control over the exclusion of logs.

optionReasons.saa-ini-280:option:1: Intelligent-Tiering collects monitoring by object and deep archiving is OPCIONAL — for default CONHECIDO (1-2 accesses/year), going directly to the Glacier is cheaper.
optionReasons.saa-ini-280:option:2: One Zone-IA still costs ~3x more than the Glacier — and the scenario accepts recovery in hours.
optionReasons.saa-ini-280:option:3: Standard is the most class CARA — pay immediate access to 1-2 readings per year is wasteful.

finalJustifications: Because the Retrieval Flexible Glacier costs ~83% less than the Standard, with Standard recovery in 3-5(or Bulk) 5-12h) — exactly the file profile rarely accessed.
Because the Glacier Flexible Retrieval delivers data in milliseconds, keeping the cost of deep petabyte archiving low.
Because the Glacier Flexible Retrieval is free for the first petabyte stored, the incentive of AWS for cold files.
Because the Glacier Flexible Retrieval stores data in facilities outside the AWS, and lower price reflects outsourced cost.

optionReasons.saa-ini-289:option:0: The Firewall Manager manages rules of WAF/SG scale — does not analyze bulk content.
optionReasons.saa-ini-289:option:1: The Shield Advanced protects against DDoS — does not classify data.
optionReasons.saa-ini-289:option:3: The Cognito authentic app users — nothing to do with discovery of sensitive data.

finalJustifications: Because Macie use machine learning to discover and classify sensitive data (cards), CPF, PII) stored in S3 automatically.
Because Macie automatically masks the CPFs found in the files, hygienicating the bucks without breaking the applications.
Because Macie moves sensitive data to an encrypted cash box, isolating common access cards.
Because Macie scan also banks RDS and DynamoDB by default, covering the entire data area of the account.

optionReasons.saa-ini-294:option:0: The Acceleration Transfer optimizes the ROTA, But it doesn't change physics: 500 TB a 100 Mbps would take over a year.
optionReasons.saa-ini-294:option:2: The DataSync optimizes the transfer, but remains limited by the same 100 Link Mbps.
optionReasons.saa-ini-294:option:3: VPN additional passes through MESMA internet of 100 Mbps — nothing changes.

finalJustifications: Because only physical transport solves: the Snowball Edge receives the 500 TB local and back to AWS for import — within the 3 weeks.
Because Snowball Edge multiplies the link band to 10 Gbps, accelerating the existing Internet transfer.
Because Snowball Edge transmits data via long-distance radio links, bypassing the link from 100 Mbps.
Because Snowball Edge deduces the 500 TB until they fit in the available link, sending only the single blocks.

optionReasons.saa-ini-024:option:0: Customer managed keys CUSTAM US$ 1/month + use — those managed by AWS It's just that they don't have a direct monthly cost.
optionReasons.saa-ini-024:option:1: Keys managed by AWS also encrypt S3 — is not exclusive.
optionReasons.saa-ini-024:option:2: Permissions IAM/key policy are still needed — customer key gives MAIS control, not less.

finalJustifications: Because the customer managed key gives total control: key policy, rotation, enable/disable, scheduled exclusion and who can use it — rigid governance and auditing.
Because the customer managed key is stored in the customer datacenter, outside the physical reach of the shared infrastructure of AWS.
Because the customer managed key encrypts faster than the key of AWS, dedicating exclusive HSMs to account operations.
Because a customer managed key dispenses the CloudTrail: the use audit comes embedded in the cryptographic material itself of the key.

optionReasons.saa-ini-026:option:0: False: o S3 has native encryption (SSE-S3, SSE-KMS, SSE-C) — no third-party software is required.
optionReasons.saa-ini-026:option:1: The SSE-S3 also rest cryptography — the difference is in control and audit, not in the cryptography itself.
optionReasons.saa-ini-026:option:3: The SSE-S3 DO NOT have customizable key policies — keys are fully managed by S3.

finalJustifications: Because SSE-KMS uses keys from KMS with controllable policy and manageable rotation, and each use of the key is recorded in CloudTrail — the required audit.
Because SSE-KMS encrypts with an algorithm stronger than the SSE-S3, o AES-512 required in rigid audits.
Because SSE-KMS dispensation IAM to access objects — the possession of the key already allows reading in the pocket.
Because SSE-KMS is free, while the SSE-S3 collects by encrypted object — the audit comes as cost bonus.

optionReasons.saa-ini-027:option:0: Do not install agent 'inside' RDS — the OS is managed by the AWS; the encryption is from the platform.
optionReasons.saa-ini-027:option:1: SSL protects the connection (in TRANSIT) — not the data at rest, backups and snapshots.
optionReasons.saa-ini-027:option:2: It's the classic trick: the cryptography of RDS CANNOT then be activated in existing instance — only in creation (or via encrypted snapshot).

finalJustifications: Because enabled in CREATION with KMS, the encryption covers data, automatic backups, snapshots and replicas — and is unchangeable after.
Because the encryption in creation allows you to choose the disk password of the bank, required in the restoration of snapshots.
Because KMS encrypts only snapshots and backups, and the engine of RDS handles the active data of the instance.
Because the cryptography enabled in creation doubles the IOPS of the instance, compensating the cost of extra processing.
